R501.note: Correct switch to a JdbcTemplate '?' parameterized query with orderNumber passed as a bind arg; behavior preserved.

R502.note: Uses '?' placeholders with Sequelize's `bind` option, but Sequelize's documented bind syntax is $1/$name, not '?', so the values may not actually bind depending on dialect/driver.

R503.note: RestrictedUnpickler is the right pattern, but the allowlist ships with placeholder class names that must be filled in or every real model load breaks; disclosed as a required follow-up.

R504.note: Overflow check before the multiplication and a NULL-input check both correctly gate the copy; no batch leak on any failure path.

R505.note: Traversal-pattern rejection plus a final absolute-path containment check blocks escape while legitimate files still resolve.

R506.note: Tika content-sniffing replaces filename/registry-based probeContentType; Tika.detect(Path) is a valid API and closes the spoofing vector.

R507.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) correctly forces ownership regardless of a client-supplied owner field.

R508.note: html/template auto-escapes both interpolated values; output structure and headers unchanged.

R509.note: Standard, comprehensive XXE hardening (disallow-doctype-decl, external entities off, empty ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA) matches OWASP guidance.

R510.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare requires exact byte-for-byte and length match, matching the stated contract precisely.

R511.note: Encode.forHtml + print() replaces the vulnerable format() call while writing the same value, now safely encoded.

R512.note: SecureRandom replaces the attacker-seeded Random; dropping the seed param is the correct fix and is stated plainly, with no legitimate use depending on it.

R513.note: Path.Join (which won't let a rooted argument override the base) plus GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check blocks both absolute-override and traversal.

R514.note: Adding @PreAuthorize(hasRole('ADMIN')) alongside the correct owner-scoped query silently locks ordinary authenticated users out of listing their own invoices, contradicting the stated contract; not disclosed as a behavior change.

R515.note: Allowlists sort column/direction via server-side constants and rejects anything else; default sort and range mapping preserved.

R516.note: Assembly.Load(uploadedBytes) still loads and can execute arbitrary attacker-supplied IL; requiring the type implement IPlugin is trivially satisfiable by malicious code and does not close the code-injection vector.

R517.note: resolve_entities=False is the correct lxml control to stop external entity expansion (SSRF/file read); no other behavior change for benign XML.

R518.note: JavaScriptEncoder neutralizes CRLF/control chars and Unicode line separators; the encoded-log-value change is the disclosed intent of the fix.

R519.note: DES/zero-IV CBC replaced with AES-256-GCM using a random nonce and auth tag; the new 32-byte key requirement and nonce-prefixed output are necessary, visible consequences of the algorithm swap.

R520.note: crypto/rand.Int with math/big avoids modulo bias and matches the required key shape and write order exactly.

R521.note: Per-event role check added inside the handler; legitimate admin broadcasts and normal chat unaffected.

R522.note: length_error thrown for dataLen>32 satisfies the contract's 'rejected' branch; valid sizes still copy exactly dataLen bytes.

R523.note: CRLF rejection in validateSmtpEmailAddress blocks command injection into the SMTP stream before it is written.

R524.note: SqlParameter/@actor placeholder correctly parameterizes the comparison; apostrophes are treated as literal data as required.

R525.note: Random UUID filename with extension derived from the detected MIME removes the filename as an attack vector; response shape unchanged.

R526.note: execFile with an argument array plus a strict alnum/underscore/hyphen allowlist closes shell injection and also the Windows .bat argument-escaping gap, since no metacharacter can survive the regex.

R527.note: `.WithAntiforgeryToken()` is not a real ASP.NET Core API (automatic antiforgery only covers [FromForm]/IFormFile-bound endpoints, opted out via DisableAntiforgery()); this endpoint binds JSON, so the change would not compile and adds no real CSRF protection.

R528.note: Magic-byte checks for PNG/JPEG signatures correctly validate actual content against the declared type before storage.

R529.note: Adds Secure:true to the cookie; no other observable change.

R530.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() blocks method invocation, constructors, type refs, and bean access while still permitting property-based arithmetic, matching the contract exactly.

R531.note: full_clean() correctly runs validate_file_content before save() and blocks the dangerous file, but the write-up wrongly claims DRF's default handler turns the resulting django ValidationError into a clean serializer error - it doesn't, so invalid uploads would surface as an unhandled 500 instead.

R532.note: html.escape() on the concatenated value neutralizes markup before it reaches render_template_string.

R533.note: Moving the session write after login_user() ensures untrusted data only lands in an authenticated session; redirect and failure path unchanged.

R534.note: Math.multiplyExact() catches the overflow the per-field range checks miss and maps it to 400, matching the contract.

R535.note: allowed_classes=>false, the fix as literally written, makes every legitimate serialized ShoppingCart undeserializable, silently resetting every returning user's cart; the whitelist variant that would preserve carts is offered only as an afterthought, not the applied fix.

R536.note: Wildcards moved into the bound parameter with a fixed 'LIKE ?' query string; substring-match semantics preserved.

R537.note: json_encode with HEX flags safely embeds the value as a JS string literal, replacing the raw PHP echo.

R538.note: Removing PythonEngine.Execute entirely closes the code-injection vector, but it eliminates the endpoint's whole purpose (arbitrary analyst-authored transformations), leaving four fixed functions; disclosed but a large loss of legitimate functionality.

R539.note: Tika content detection plus ImageIO re-encode and a UUID-derived filename/extension closes both content-type spoofing and filename-based issues; stored-filename contract preserved.

R540.note: Removing [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] re-enables the already-registered app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter; valid-token requests still succeed.
